messages:
ashok: Heads up — spike in GPU provisioning failures in eu-west-1. Lots of CreateNode errors with KMS decrypt timeouts right after the egress firewall tweak at ~03:15 UTC. Is oncall aware?

sre-oncall: saw the pagers, putting mitigations in motion. KMS client TLS handshakes are resetting. Looks like privatelink/e2e to keystore is being blocked intermittently. Investigating network traces.

dana-sec: we rolled out a tightened egress posture last night to block agent/3p callbacks. Keystore endpoints were on the allowlist — did something change in the NACLs or firewall rules? @maria-infra any recent updates?

maria-infra: we did tighten egress NACL + firewall to remove broad 0.0.0.0/0 allows for instance subnets and route keystore traffic through the proxy/NAT. The keystore NAT has a strict allowlist to keystore.redwoodkms.com (443), but some nodes are resolving CNAMEs to different IPs because of DNS TTLs.

ashok: logs show attempts to connect to additional IP ranges used by the CA chain and CRL checks — KMS client briefly opens to multiple endpoints during TLS. If those IPs are blocked, the client falls back but times out.

ryan-sre: short-term: add ephemeral egress allow for the observed IP ranges + enable VPC endpoint for KMS. Long-term: privatelink is ideal. I'll draft the change.

maria-infra: we can stand up a KMS privatelink in eu-west-1 but it needs an account-level endpoint policy and cross-account routing. That requires security signoff. @dana-sec can you fast-track approval for dev/prod?

dana-sec: I can approve a scoped privatelink if we attach a restrictive endpoint policy, pin DNS to the VPC endpoint, and enable audit logging for all KMS API calls. I also need the last 24h of egress flow logs + CloudTrail KMS events for compliance review.

ashok: cost note — fallback plan to route provisioning to us-west-2 adds ~120ms latency and increases warm-pool holding costs. If we keep a warm pool cross-region it could add ~ $1800–$2400/day at current instance sizes. For provisioning retries the main hit is queue time, not token cost.

ryan-sre: current impact metrics: provisioning failure rate ~12% this morning, leading to reduced effective GPU capacity during peak ramp. Can we enable a narrowly scoped NAT bypass for the provisioning subnets while we put privatelink in place?

maria-infra: I'll prepare a time-limited ACL change to allow only the observed KMS + CA IP ranges from the gpu-provisioning tag. Command I'll run (patching firewall):

```bash
gcloud compute firewall-rules update allow-kms-egress \
  --allow tcp:443 \
  --source-tags gpu-provisioning \
  --direction=EGRESS \
  --destination-ranges 13.35.0.0/16,52.95.0.0/16 \
  --description "temp allow for KMS handshake + CA certs, auto-revoke in 6h"
```

dana-sec: fine with time-limited rule, but add two guardrails: 1) automated revoke at 6h, 2) Sigma alert if any gpu-provisioning host tries to connect to destinations outside the allowlist. Also confirm CloudTrail+flowlogs capture the KMS API calls in that period. Enable KMS key access logging immediately.

ashok: I'll add a CMA to track warm-pool spend and alert if cross-region warm pool cost estimate crosses $1500/day. Also scheduling a Draining rollout to free stalled provisioning once privatelink is live.

deploy-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-493 — eu-west1 KMS egress block affecting GPU provisioning. Assignees: maria-infra, ryan-sre, dana-sec, ashok.

maria-infra: applying the temporary rule now, will report back in ~5m with provisioning success counts and egress logs.

ryan-sre: after the change provisioning success rate jumped to ~98%. Keeping incident open until privatelink + endpoint policy + audit is confirmed.
